From abbd00b82a2771b0460ba2cffdb1343aa827ccde Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Wolfgang Grandegger <wg@grandegger.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Nov 2011 14:30:05 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] net/can/mscan: Fix buggy listen only mode setting

This patch fixes an issue introduced recently with commit
452448f9283e1939408b397e87974a418825b0a8.

CC: Marc Kleine-Budde <mkl@pengutronix.de>
Signed-off-by: Wolfgang Grandegger <wg@grandegger.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/drivers/net/can/mscan/mscan.c b/drivers/net/can/mscan/mscan.c
index 74f3b1829e02..1c82dd8b896e 100644
--- a/drivers/net/can/mscan/mscan.c
+++ b/drivers/net/can/mscan/mscan.c
@@ -581,7 +581,7 @@ static int mscan_open(struct net_device *dev)
 
 	priv->open_time = jiffies;
 
-	if (ctrlmode.flags & CAN_CTRLMODE_LISTENONLY)
+	if (priv->can.ctrlmode & CAN_CTRLMODE_LISTENONLY)
 		setbits8(&regs->canctl1, MSCAN_LISTEN);
 	else
 		clrbits8(&regs->canctl1, MSCAN_LISTEN);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/net/can/mscan/mscan.c`**
- The condition for setting the listen-only mode has been modified. 
- The original line:
  ```c
  if (ctrlmode.flags & CAN_CTRLMODE_LISTENONLY)
  ```
  has been changed to:
  ```c
  if (priv->can.ctrlmode & CAN_CTRLMODE_LISTENONLY)
  ```
- This change ensures that the listen-only mode is determined based on the `priv->can.ctrlmode` instead of `ctrlmode.flags`.

### Relationships
- The modification in `mscan.c` addresses a bug introduced by a previous commit (identified by the hash `452448f9283e1939408b397e87974a418825b0a8`). The patch corrects the logic for enabling the listen-only mode, ensuring that the correct variable (`priv->can.ctrlmode`) is used to check the mode instead of the outdated `ctrlmode.flags`. This change is crucial for the proper functioning of the CAN device in listen-only mode.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (ctrlmode.flags & CAN_CTRLMODE_LISTENONLY)
```
Reason:
The incorrect variable `ctrlmode.flags` was used to check for the listen-only mode instead of the correct `priv->can.ctrlmode`. This mistake caused the system to improperly handle the listen-only mode setting, potentially leading to the CAN device not functioning correctly when it was supposed to be in that mode.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (priv->can.ctrlmode & CAN_CTRLMODE_LISTENONLY)
```
Reason:
By changing the check to use `priv->can.ctrlmode`, the code now correctly verifies the listen-only mode setting. This ensures that the CAN device behaves as intended when it is supposed to be in listen-only mode, thus fixing the bug.
